title: Quasi-Non-Hermitian Edge Bursts Induced by Nonuniform Loss
authors: Ze Yang, Wei Li, Fuxiang Li
abstract: Non-Hermitian quantum walks on lossy lattices with open boundaries can exhibit an anomalous peak of the loss probability at the boundary, known as the non-Hermitian edge burst (NHEB). This phenomenon has been attributed to the combined effect of the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) and a gapless imaginary spectrum. Here we investigate a class of models in which the NHSE is induced by magnetic flux while the loss is spatially nonuniform. We show that the spatial distribution of loss plays a crucial role in determining the emergence and strength of the NHEB. Notably, even in the absence of the NHSE, a weak boundary accumulation of the loss probability persists. We term this effect a quasi-non-Hermitian edge burst (quasi-NHEB). By analyzing the dependence of the loss probability on the initial position, we further demonstrate that the quasi-NHEB obeys a bulk-edge scaling relation distinct from that of conventional NHEB. Our results show that spatially nonuniform loss alone can generate boundary-localized loss anomalies even without the NHSE, providing new insight into non-Hermitian boundary phenomena and a broader platform for their exploration and potential applications.
summary: The paper explores non-Hermitian quantum walks on lattices with spatially varying dissipation. It introduces the concept of a quasi-NHEB, demonstrating that nonuniform loss alone can create anomalous boundary loss accumulation even without the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect. This highlights that structured dissipation offers an independent and powerful control mechanism for engineering edge physics.
main_problem: The study investigates non-Hermitian boundary phenomena, specifically how spatially nonuniform loss influences the Non-Hermitian Edge Burst (NHEB) in quantum walks.
main_result: Spatially nonuniform loss alone can generate a quasi-non-Hermitian edge burst ($	ext{quasi-NHEB}$) even when the system lacks the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect (NHSE).
method: The analysis involves simulating quantum walker dynamics on a tight-binding lattice, calculating the boundary loss probability ($P_x$), and comparing scaling relations between different non-Hermiticity regimes.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional non-Hermitian tight-binding chain with two coupled sublattices (A and B). Non-Hermiticity arises from imaginary on-site loss ($\gamma_x$) on sublattice B, which can be made spatially nonuniform and influenced by an artificial magnetic flux ($\phi$).
key_observables: Loss probability distribution ($P_x$), Mean Inverse Participation Ratio ($	ext{MIPR}$), Non-Hermitian Edge Burst (NHEB) magnitude, and the dependence of boundary loss on initial position ($x_0$).
important_parameters: Magnetic flux ($\phi$), spatial gradient/variation of loss ($\gamma_x$), and the comparison between uniform vs. nonuniform loss regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on open boundary conditions for the quantum walk, and it distinguishes between phenomena driven by NHSE versus those driven purely by inhomogeneous dissipation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic lattice setup with site-dependent loss; they show $	ext{MIPR}$ vs. flux to diagnose NHSE, and spatial maps of the loss probability ($P_x$) comparing uniform, quasi-, and conventional edge bursts under varying fluxes and loss gradients.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates three regimes: (i) Quasi-NHEB induced by nonuniform loss at zero flux ($\phi=0$); (ii) Hybrid NHEB resulting from the interplay of NHSE and nonuniform loss ($\phi=-\pi/2$); and (iii) Comparison against the conventional NHEB found in uniform loss models. The structure builds the argument that dissipation gradient is a key control parameter.
why_interesting: This work provides a generalized framework for understanding boundary effects beyond standard topological invariants, showing how engineered disorder (nonuniform loss) can independently induce robust edge phenomena.
